rv.q: At the Garrick, the production is finally being seen and heard at its best.
But the conceptual framing that makes it special is also a limitation.
All of which is a long prelude to admitting The Last Five Years leaves me both dazzled and entirely disconnected.
Lynch and Higginson together are sensational, better even than they were at the Southwark Playhouse, and it’s impossible to imagine two greater performances in the West End right now.
Audiences will lap up the melodies, singing and storyline.
As had the rest of the very young West End audience with an average age of, I'd say, 27, who stood and cheered this production of The Last Five Years to the rafters.
Brown’s bitter-sweet score is always pleasant to listen to.
The Last Five Years really is a slice of perfection.
Jonathan O’Boyle’s slick direction flawlessly bonds all the different performance elements of The Last Five Years into one immersive whole piece.
It’s disappointing as The Last Five Years has a lot of individually strong elements, but it never feels like it adds up to more than the sum of its parts.

cn.t: Brown's cult musical finally reaches the West End with strong performances and beautiful melodies, though critics remain divided on whether this bittersweet two-hander fully transcends its intimate origins.
